newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military readies for move to Miami.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military readies for move to Miami.

text.p: The U.S. Southern Command heaquarters will house the military's most sophisticated communications systems when it moves to Miami from Panama later this year, SOUTHCOM commander General Wesley Clark said on Friday.
Clarke signed a phased occupancy lease and toured the newly constructed headquarters building located at a business park west of Miami airport on Friday.
Most of 900 personnel will move from Quarry Heights, Panama, in September after the new headquarters are furnished and the communications systems are installed.
"It's going to be the most advanced communications centre of the U.S. army anywhere in the world," Clarke said at the signing ceremony.

Southern Command controls all U.S. military activity and national security interests in Latin America south of Mexico. In June it also will assume responsibilty for the Caribbean, reflecting the key role it plays in the war against drugs trafficking.

In the 1980s SOUTHCOM was primarliy concerned with opposing Communist insurgents in Central America, Clark said. Now the focus had shifted to fighting Latin American drugs traffickers, in which the military acted in support of other U.S. government agencies, he said.
It also worked to encourage Latin American militaries to support democratic rule and respect human rights, he said.
Clarke said Miami was the ideal place for SOUTHCOM to relocate because of its social, cultural, economic and communications links to Latin America. "We will be good neighbours to Miami," he said.

SOUTHCOM traces its origins to 1903, when U.S. marines landed in Panama to protect the railroad across the isthmus. They stayed to guard the Panama Canal when it was built. It has been based at Quarry Heights since 1942.
